Subject: Re: RFP Addendum: Updated Subprocessor Roster + NebulaEdge — Security Summary

Soojin / team — quick summary from Security & Trust for the packet:

Executive summary:
- NebulaEdge is a regional edge operator we pilot in select EU regions (eu-west-1). It acts as a TCP/GRPC edge cache and does not have direct access to our model weights or storage buckets.
- Data-in-transit: traffic between Redwood and NebulaEdge is encrypted (mTLS). NebulaEdge does not perform decryption of payloads beyond TLS termination at the edge; on-path encrypted payloads are forwarded to our regional gateway where payloads are processed inside our controlled VPCs.
- KMS: Redwood controls all customer encryption keys used for tokenization and persistent storage. NebulaEdge does not hold KMS keys. For ephemeral session-level TLS keys, NebulaEdge manages termination certificates but never holds long-term customer encryption material.
- Logging: NebulaEdge collects operational metadata (latency, packet headers) but does not persist request bodies. Any logs that may contain sensitive metadata are redacted before retention.

Evidence & attachments included for RFP:
- nebulaedge-sla.pdf (edge operator MSA + security addendum)
- nebulaedge-kms-diagram.png (network + KMS boundary diagram)
- soc2-report-2025-type2.pdf (Redwood SOC 2 Type II summary we can share under NDA)

Open items / caveats:
- We allow customers to opt out of NebulaEdge routing per account (routing control in Console). If Acme requires strict exclusion, we can provide account-level config to prevent edge routing to NebulaEdge.
- NebulaEdge is contractually constrained from persisting payloads — evidence is in the SLA, but this is an operator that does TLS termination at the edge in exchange for latency gains.

I will attach the files to the compiled packet and include a short "change notice" paragraph for procurement.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Trust (Redwood Inference)
